svg.aria-label: The rollout as rollout.py builds it, the same code on every site with the policy from the site's rollout.yaml. Stage 1, plan, read-only and so on production too: every host is read live, in parallel, in a session of about 10 to 30 GETs: the service root, systems, managers and chassis, the UpdateService with its firmware inventory and SimpleUpdate ActionInfo, tasks and jobs, and each reset's ActionInfo. The image is fetched once from the site's cache into the spool and its sha256 compared with images.yaml. Pre-flight decides go, skip or block, every check recorded: a skip is nothing to do now or busy, try a later wave; a block needs a person: no live read, health not OK, a failed job or task, a downgrade or an order it can't tell without --allow-downgrade, Updateable false, under LowestSupportedVersion, no image or a wrong sha256 or size, no image of the running version to reinstall without --accept-no-rollback, a host reset with no drain set, no update service or no way in. The hosts that pass go into a canary per model and waves by cumulative percentage, at most max_per_rack of a rack in a wave; plan.json freezes the inputs' sha256, the policy, the waves and each verdict with the BMC's identity. Each stage then refuses changed inputs, --halt-at and any host not writable, and without --yes is a dry run. Every host of a wave, max_parallel at once: 1 pre-flight again on a fresh read, the BMC the one the plan read; 2 drain, only when the reset restarts the host, by rollout.yaml's command, skipped in the lab; 3 update, a multipart push of the spooled file or a SimpleUpdate pull of a URL, with Targets and OperationApplyTime OnReset, the Task followed until it ends; 4 reset, the Manager or ComputerSystem reset that activates it, GracefulRestart first, and a wait until it is back; 5 post-check on a fresh read, the target version, health OK or no worse, no new failed job or task; 6 undrain. A failure before the reset is failed, the old firmware still runs. After it, the rollback reinstalls the version from before with steps 3 to 5; verified is rolled_back, otherwise needs_attention and kept drained. After a wave its updated hosts soak and are post-checked again, then the gate: the canary and the first strict waves halt on any failure, any wave on a soak failure, later waves over halt_at. Every step is recorded twice, intent before and result after, in the run record, sent to Loki and pushed as metrics to the Pushgateway; the report is built from the plan and the records. Not built: a JobService handoff, Activate and staged images, EventService events, an A/B bank switch, host locks and resuming a stopped run.
